The treatment plan outlined for acute bacterial sinusitis is appropriate and aligns with current clinical guidelines. Amoxicillin-clavulanate is considered a first-line antibiotic therapy for acute bacterial rhinosinusitis, particularly in patients who have failed initial therapy or are at higher risk for resistant organisms. The 10-day duration is consistent with standard recommendations for adults. Nasal saline irrigation is a recommended adjunctive therapy to help clear mucus and reduce inflammation. Oral decongestants may be used for symptomatic relief, although their efficacy is variable and they should be used cautiously. The advice to return if symptoms persist beyond seven days or worsen is prudent, as it allows for reassessment of the diagnosis (to rule out viral etiology or complications) and potential adjustment of therapy.
